name: AWQ INT3-g128 WikiText-2 perplexity delta vs fp16, OPT-6.7B
unit: perplexity_delta (WikiText-2 ppl points, quantized minus FP16)
methodology: AWQ paper Table 3. Model OPT-6.7B, weight-only INT3, group size 128, activations FP16. Metric: WikiText-2 perplexity in the AWQ harness. FP16 baseline 10.86; AWQ INT3-g128 scores 11.39. The same table lists plain round-to-nearest at 23.54, a 'keep 1 percent of weights in fp16' mixed-precision variant at 11.39, and a fixed s=2 rescale at 11.92.
notes: DELTA = +0.53 ppl (11.39 vs 10.86). This is the record that shows why the delta must be stated against fp16 and never against RTN. Naive RTN at the same 3-bit precision costs +12.68 ppl (23.54 vs 10.86) - a number that makes 3-bit quantization look impossible. The quantizer choice is worth 12.15 ppl of that, i.e. the folk memory '3-bit destroys the model' is the RTN cell, not the format. Second trap: the protection is not monotone. The paper's scaling sweep on this exact model (Table 2) gives 23.54 at s=1, 12.87 at s=1.25, 12.48 at s=1.5, 11.92 at s=2 and 12.36 at s=4 - the optimum is interior, because scaling salient channels harder also inflates the group max Delta and damages the non-salient 97 percent. 'Protect the outliers harder' is not a free dial.
